interpretation.explanation: The R&D premium does not concentrate in hard-to-arbitrage stocks. This pattern is more consistent with a risk-based explanation: high R&D firms have higher expected returns because they are exposed to innovation risk that investors dislike.

transaction_costs.methodology_note: Transaction costs estimated using Novy-Marx & Velikov (2016) methodology. Assumes annual rebalancing, 40% annual turnover, and SP500 liquidity characteristics.

annual_hml_premium.note: Annual non-overlapping HML premium with Newey-West SE. July-June convention (preferred).

methodology.formation_rule: FY(T-1) R&D data -> Returns July T to June T+1

turnover.note: Turnover is computed as 0.5 * sum |w_t - w_{t-1}|. First year turnover reflects initial formation and is excluded from averages.

cost_assumptions.note: Net-of-cost series is a simple approximation: annual trading cost is proportional to realized turnover using literature-calibrated cost parameters.

5yr.interpretation: The gross R&D premium of 5.4% becomes 5.4% after accounting for estimated trading costs of 0.07% annually.

interpretation.summary: R&D premium is NOT fully explained by standard factors (alpha is significant)
interpretation.recommendation: The evidence suggests R&D intensity may represent a distinct pricing factor.

double_sort_analysis.interpretation: The R&D premium is significant among small-cap firms (spread = 9.83%, t = 5.47), and significant among large-cap firms (spread = 3.2%, t = 2.48). This confirms that R&D intensity captures return-relevant information beyond what is explained by firm size.

methodology_notes.formation_rule: FY(T) characteristics -> Returns July(T+1) to June(T+2)

delisting_sensitivity.note: Simulated sensitivity using literature-calibrated delisting adjustments (Shumway 1997, Beaver et al. 2007). Actual CRSP delisting returns not available in this dataset.

moderate.description: Literature midpoint: typical delisting adjustment for S&P 500.

aggressive.description: Literature upper bound: assumes higher distress exit rate differential.

conservative.description: Literature lower bound: minimal delisting effect for large-cap universe.
